text:
katie: heads-up — nightly training on g5-cluster-2 hit repeated NCCL allreduce stalls around 03:10 UTC, p99 token-sync up ~10s. filing here because it looks network-y :frowning:
infra-bot: alert: nccl_allreduce_latency > 2s on job/train-237 (node: g5-12,g5-13)
ram: thanks — which nodes exactly? screenshots/logs?
katie: g5-12 (pod gpu-0..7) -> g5-13 (gpu-0..7). happened ~03:09-03:13, multiple jobs affected.
alice: quick grep of kube logs shows a string of ibv events on g5-13:
```
[ 03:09:12 ] IBV_EVENT_QP_FATAL on qp 0x1a2
[ 03:09:13 ] mlx5_core: mlx5 0000:81:00.1: port 1 xmit timeout
```
sanjay: any recent kernel/firmware rollouts to that AZ? mlx5 fw was updated last week.
ram: yes, we rolled mlx5 fw 17.28 -> 19.01 on 2115549400 across pool-b to pick up sq doorbell perf fix.
katie: interesting — the timing matches.
alice: tcpdump from g5-12 shows lots of VXLAN fragments (outer UDP) + ICMP unreachable for large packets. gist:
```
03:09:10.123 IP g5-12 > g5-13: UDP, len 65535
03:09:10.123 IP g5-13 > g5-12: ICMP frag needed and DF set, mtu 9000
```
ram: so PMTU discovery failing -> large RDMA/UDP encaps packets get dropped and we see reorder/fragmentation.
sanjay: also saw kernel dmesg on g5-13 complaining GSO not supported on VF: "net: VF eth0: can't do GSO (SG)"
alice: that plus SR-IOV VFs + VXLAN path -> host offloads mismatch. when hw segmentation offload is disabled on VF, VXLAN sends big UDPs that expect GSO, fragmentation occurs and some ToR drops fragments due to an older ASIC bug.
katie: NCCL reacts poorly to persistent out-of-order/lost packets and falls back/blocks, hence the stalls.
ram: runbook idea: disable VXLAN on the RDMA path or force MTU < 1500 on the overlay, or toggle VF offload flags. short-term: add tc egress-mtu clamp for pods to 1450.
sanjay: I'll spin up a repro with ib_write_bw and iperf with --mtu/--df to validate. also will test with VF ethtool -K to turn off gso/gro and then re-enable.
alice: commands I ran:
```
# on g5-13
etstat -s | grep -i icmp
ethtool -k eth0 | egrep "gso|gro|tso"
cat /sys/class/net/eth0/mtu
```
katie: quick mitigation applied: infra applied a k8s networkpolicy that pins RDMA pods to host-interfaces (bypass vxlan) for the affected node pool, immediate p99 dropped from 10s -> 0.6s.
ram: good rollback plan? if firmware is root cause we should pin to previous fw on critical pools until vendor fix.
sanjay: filed ticket with NIC vendor + ToR vendor (case #RNW-4891). attaching pcap and dmesg.
alice: note: this only reproduced when the node had SR-IOV VFs enabled and a mixed kernel 5.15/5.19 fleet (we still have a few 5.15 nodes). mixing kernels + new fw seems to trigger different offload paths.
katie: action items: 1) sanjay - repro + vendor ticket (owner) 2) ram - add short-term tc mtuchain to k8s net-attach for rdma pods 3) alice - gather per-node ethtool/ibv counters and attach to ticket. will check back in 24h.
ram: acked. added a quick TC rule on the staggers: `tc qdisc add dev eth0 clsact` + `tc egress change ...` (note: will paste exact later)
infra-bot: incident created: RNW-4891, severity: medium, owner: sanjay
katie: thanks all — kept jobs running by routing RDMA traffic off-vxlan. please paste repro steps here when ready.
